# Jack/Jason Catch Up
Date: 2026-10-27 | Duration: 21.06999969482422m

## Summary
The discussion covered a transition toward Growth Book as Deadwater winds down into maintenance, with Aaron handling operations while on parental leave and no client closings planned. Airtop’s shutdown is scheduled for November 13; signups and upgrades have stopped, existing accounts remain accessible, and users must migrate workflows. Messaging, signup, and reliability issues contributed to Airtop’s product-market concerns, while Amir repeatedly rejected marketing recommendations. The Growth Book role reports to Ashley and focuses on operations, website and content ownership, and internal coordination rather than generic marketing. A small team is planned eventually, with Emmy interested in product management. The content program emphasizes internal voices, lightweight editing, pull-request summaries, and automated accuracy checks. Six or seven review layers, limited reviewer capacity, six-article monthly output, launch pressure, and Monday 9 AM meetings create execution friction, while consulting offers faster build-and-ship work without people management or daily standups.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Deadwater, Airtop shutdown, Content operations, Approval bottlenecks, AI fact-checking

## Action Items
**Jack Virag**
Continue winding Deadwater (01:00)
Route Deadwater inquiries to Aaron (01:00)
Develop GrowthBook content programme (15:03)
Publish GrowthBook content programme (15:03)
